caption: Elijah’s ascent can meaningfully illustrate Jesus’s ascension. Luke may reuse the pattern—but Second Kings tells Elijah’s story, not a spoken forecast about Jesus.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Does Elijah illustrate Jesus’s ascension? Elijah goes up into heaven before Elisha. Luke later says Jesus was carried into heaven before his disciples.
slides.body: Elijah goes up into heaven before Elisha. Luke later says Jesus was carried into heaven before his disciples.
slides.heading: Does Elijah illustrate Jesus’s ascension?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of 2Kgs 2:11: Elijah went up into heaven in a whirlwind.
slides.body: Elijah went up into heaven in a whirlwind.
slides.heading: 2Kgs 2:11

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Lk 24:51, BSB: While He was blessing them, He left them and was carried up into heaven.
slides.body: While He was blessing them, He left them and was carried up into heaven.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Lk 24:51

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: The wider pattern is meaningful Both departures pass a mission to followers who receive spiritual power. Luke uses Elijah stories elsewhere too.
slides.body: Both departures pass a mission to followers who receive spiritual power. Luke uses Elijah stories elsewhere too.
slides.heading: The wider pattern is meaningful

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: It is a pattern, not a forecast Elijah’s ascent is an event in his own life. Luke may reuse its shape without treating it as a spoken prophecy.
slides.body: Elijah’s ascent is an event in his own life. Luke may reuse its shape without treating it as a spoken prophecy.
slides.heading: It is a pattern, not a forecast

title: Elijah's ascent
